subject: Follow-up: Incident summary & RCA for May 15th service disruption
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@cascadehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 16 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Incident summary & RCA for May 15th service disruption

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for your patience while we finished our internal investigation into the May 15th disruption that affected your production inference endpoints for ~42 minutes. I wanted to share an initial summary and confirm we'll deliver a concise RCA document and timeline by EOD Monday.

High-level summary (short):
- Impact: intermittent 5xx errors and increased latency on your primary endpoint between 22:11–22:53 UTC on 2026-05-15.
- Root cause (short): a cascading autoscaler bug combined with a timing regression in our batching layer which led to a scheduler deadlock under a specific traffic burst pattern.
- Immediate mitigation: we rolled to the previous autoscaler build and applied a hotfix to guard batching slot allocation; traffic normalized and error rates returned to baseline.

We're attaching a short RCA summary and a timeline CSV; the full write-up will include action items, mitigations, and planned preventative releases. If you need an executive-ready one-page summary for your SOC/Procurement team, say the word and we'll produce it.

I'm available to run through this on a quick call if you'd like (30m). Proposed slots: Mon 10:00–11:00 PT or Mon 15:00–16:00 PT.

Apologies again for the disruption — we'll make sure our fixes reduce the risk of recurrence and are clear about any work that touches your SLAs.

Best,
Markus Klein
Sr. Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0182

Attachments: cascade_rca_summary_May15.pdf (RCA summary, 2 pages); incident_timeline_May15.csv (event timestamps).

Markus,

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the summary. A couple quick questions from our side:
- Was any customer data read or written incorrectly during the window? We need to know if there was lateral data exposure risk.
- Do you have the exact request IDs / traces for our affected calls so our SREs can cross-reference?

We appreciate the attachment — we'll review and reach out with any compliance questions. We can do Monday 10:00 PT for a call. Please confirm.

– Elena
Director of IT Operations, Cascade Health
elena@cascadehealth.com

On a related note, please include any mitigation timelines you plan for prevention — our security team needs to update our vendor risk register.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 16 May 2026 13:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Incident summary & RCA for May 15th service disruption

Thanks — forwarding Elena's questions. Quick internal notes:
- Data exposure: preliminary check shows no PII exfiltration and no cross-tenant read; logs confirm request routing stayed within tenant isolation boundaries. Will validate with security logs and paste trace IDs.
- Traces: SUP-3491 has the full trace bundle; I'll extract trace ids for Cascade and drop them into the shared Drive doc.
- Action items I recommend we include in the customer-facing RCA: timeline, root cause narrative, immediate remediation, permanent code fix ETA, and compensatory actions (credit/offering).

I'll prepare the executive summary doc and the detailed technical annex. Markus: do you want us to mention the planned release window for the autoscaler fix (we have a tent. target Wed May 21st)?

Marissa
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

P.S. tagging Lauren for any legal/contractual notes re: SLA credit wording.

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@cascadehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Final RCA & next steps (May 15 outage)

Elena —

Attached is the full RCA and timeline for the May 15th outage (cascade_rca_summary_May15.pdf, incident_timeline_May15.csv). Below is a concise customer-facing summary we shared with our security/compliance teams and that you can distribute internally.

1) What happened (concise):
At 22:11 UTC on 2026-05-15 a burst of concurrent requests to several model endpoints triggered an edge case in our autoscaler that caused a race between worker de-registration and batch-slot reclamation. Under the specific traffic pattern, this led to a scheduler deadlock and temporary backlog growth that produced 5xx responses while the system attempted to recover.

2) Impact:
- Duration: 22:11–22:53 UTC (42 minutes)
- Affect: ~0.9% of requests to your production endpoint returned 5xx; average latency spiked for packets that encountered the deadlock path. No retries were dropped by Redwood.

3) Data risk:
- Our investigation found no evidence of data leakage or cross-tenant access. All requests and KV state remained logically separated. Full log export and trace IDs for your calls are attached.

4) Immediate remediation taken:
- Rolled back the autoscaler change that introduced the regression.
- Deployed a hotfix to batching allocation to prevent slot starvation.
- Increased monitoring and anomaly alerts for batch queue length and worker de-registration latency.

5) Permanent fixes & timeline:
- Engineering will ship autoscaler race condition fix in w/c 2026-05-18 with an internal canary on Tue 2026-05-19 and full rollout Wed 2026-05-21 (target).
- We will add an additional integration test that simulates the specific traffic pattern and include it in our CI gate.

6) Preventative & compensatory actions:
- Add a post-deploy canary for autoscaler builds to detect regressions earlier.
- Quarterly configuration review with your SREs to tune batching and burst handling.
- As a gesture for the disruption we can offer a 1% credit for May invoice or a package of free throughput credits — let us know which you prefer.

7) Ask of Cascade Health:
If you can share a representative request sample (anonymized) of the traffic profile that triggered the burst, that will help us harden the test case. We can accept it via secure upload link — see Drive doc.

Next steps:
- I propose a 30-minute call today at 10:00 PT to walk through the attached docs and the rollout plan.
- We'll keep the Jira ticket SUP-3491 updated with timestamps and deployment notes.

Apologies again for the disruption and thank you for the clear questions — we'll prioritize preventing recurrence.

Best regards,
Markus Klein
Sr. Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachments: cascade_rca_summary_May15.pdf; incident_timeline_May15.csv
Related links: SUP-3491 (https://redwood-inference.atlassian.net/browse/SUP-3491); RCA doc https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c-rca-cascade

We can provide an anonymized traffic sample by end of day Wednesday; please send the secure upload link and instructions. We'll plan to take you up on the quarterly configuration review.

10:00 PT for the call works for our team. See you then.

Regards,
Elena
